W2 (empirical), after E045. Tip is E036: 5.314 s, 0.7532 on seeds 0-2; fresh seeds 13-22 gave 0.7525. Identical code re-runs (E043 0.7497, E038 0.7525) show rebuild noise of about 0.3 pp on a 3-seed mean, so a 3-seed read near 0.753 is a coin flip. Population mean is about 0.752, leaving about 0.2 pp of headroom over the 0.75 bar.

Mechanisms, with the experiments that support them:
1. Epoch dial: about 5% of time per 0.5 epoch, for 0.0-0.25 pp (E020, E023, E027). E034 stacked the freeze with +0.5 epoch and saved 0.40 s vs E027 at about 0 pp.
2. EMA (+0.97 pp, E005) and Muon (+0.66 pp, confounded, E006) are in the tip. More than 10 time-neutral boosters failed (E025, E029, E030, E032, E044, wd, LS). Averaging, LR shape and wd sit at a flat optimum within about 0.2 pp. BN recalibration (E044) showed no gain.
3. Time tracks pixels. Early low resolution is nearly free up to about 30% at 20 px (E026, E033). E040 saved about 0.12 s and cost 0.06-0.28 pp. E041 (12-step trim) cost about 0.2 pp. E045 (smaller early batch) cost +0.2 s and gained nothing measurable.
4. Backward truncation was the best lever (E028, E034, E036). E037 (freeze at 60%) saved 0.25 s but cost 0.38 pp. E039 and E042 saved only 0.03-0.05 s. The stem is nearly exhausted. Group 2 is the remaining target, but a freeze late in the run has a short window.
5. Loss-based dropping (E031) and fewer steps cost about 1.5-2.3 s per pp, about the same rate as the epoch dial.
6. Noise: 3-seed accuracy std is about 0.15-0.2 pp, and any RNG or step-count change reshuffles it. Time noise is about 0.5%, or about ±0.03 s near 5.3 s.

Misses: accuracy fell below my point when training signal was cut. Time-neutral boosters were over-predicted. Rebuilds shifted accuracy by 0.3 pp (E043). Time was usually right; E043 fell just outside a range I set too narrow.

Unsure: whether bandwidth-bound levers transfer to the PCIe judge, whether padding to 32 channels gives more than 2%, and whether a group-2 freeze is neutral. A 10% freeze window of about 23 steps at group-2 backward cost (about 25% of a 32 px step) gives a saving of at most about 0.06 s.

forecasts.reason: The freeze window is only about 23 steps, so the saving is roughly 0.05 s, which is at the noise floor. Accuracy is likely to lose 0.0-0.15 pp.
It is a diagnostic with no recipe change. The numbers are just a re-run of the tip, and the profiling would show whether conv1 is inefficient.
Dropping 5% of the samples saves about 4-5% of time, as E031 did. Accuracy is expected to lose about 0.1-0.15 pp, which is on the dial's rate and within noise.
The math is identical, so accuracy is rebuild noise only. Padding to 32 channels might save 0-2%, but the saving is uncertain because the cuDNN kernels may already pad internally.

cruxes: How much of a 32 px step does group-2 backward actually cost, and how many steps could it be frozen for without accuracy loss? That sets the ceiling of I070 at roughly 0.05 s.
Does padding the conv1 input from 24 to 32 channels change kernel selection? That decides whether I073 gives more than 2%, or nothing.
What is the 20-seed population mean for E036? If it is below 0.752, time cuts are no longer affordable.
